doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Woody on Hanna and Dave Tough, Don Lamond
summary: Woody praised Hanna's tempos; Hanna on Don Lamond and Dave Tough; Herman's unpaid money and the IRS.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Someone said something about you in the Herman band is that when you were with them they could play tempos that they had never been able to play.
Oh Woody, yeah, Woody said that. And that was the only difference between me and the other guys, Dave and Don, he said, “Yeah we can play any tempo with Jake.” He actually

could play any tempo with Don too you know. He could play any tempo, Don Lamond, he’s phenomenal. He’s the greatest big band drummer of all time for my money. And with Dave, he had two tempos. He’d either come down on the one or go up into the other. And once he got there, you never heard anything like that. But otherwise —
This is Dave Tough you’re talking about?

Dave Tough, yeah. You had to glide into one tempo or go out into — he had two favorite tempos and he’d bring that band into one of those things by about the second chorus, it was roaring, once you get this time right there, he was phenomenal that guy. That’s the hottest swinging drummer I ever heard. I never heard a guy swing that hard.
Yeah. Woody said, “Jake is the first great big band drummer to come along since Dave Tough.”
Yeah? Wow. That’s all right. I like Woody a little better now.

I don’t mind he beat me out of that money. I don’t mind that. It’s worth it. Worth it he said that. I’d rather have the money, but anyway, I’m glad. Of course he didn’t have the money to pay anyway, what the hell? He was broker than I was. We didn’t know that though.
Oh that poor guy had some problems, didn’t he?
Oh those people are merciless, the IRS. They’re finally going after the IRS. It’s about time. Oh they can get real mean you know.
